verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A faster insert grade shortens cycle time on its own, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant.

The reported rates cover a narrower population than the claim: "Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol." A quarter of each ward's patients are dropped, so the 6-11 percent falls describe a selected fully-compliant subgroup rather than the ward's infection rate.

The figures cover a narrower population than the claim: "Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices." One fifth of each line's orders are excluded, so the 4-7 percent rise is for a selected subset of orders, not the line's revenue per order.

Two of the four cases measure the outcome before the intervention started: cohort One "started 4 April; by 29 March resting heart rate ran 5 bpm below" and cohort Three "started 5 October; by 30 September ... 6 bpm below". The drop precedes enrolment, so the app cannot have caused it.
